“The inspection list is clean again, which means I can sleep. But I keep coming back to that audit report — first cycle, D7 office, public portal. Numbers are the only thing that don't lie to you, but they don't tell you if Mrs. Okafor can actually get her blood pressure checked without taking two buses. We built the damn building, that part's done. Now we've got to prove it works, every quarter, on paper, in public. That's the job now. Fine. I'd rather be accountable than comfortable.” — Bobby

“Four cycles of visioning, and still the same knot in my stomach: we've got the blueprints, the budget line, even the consultant picked—but no vote, no shovels. I keep going back to Doña Esperanza's cart on the renderings, making sure the diagonal path doesn't clip her awning, because that's the part people will actually feel. “The C115 review is next week, and I keep coming back to the fact that the soil verification is the one thing we can point to that’s truly done. No more debate about whether the ground is clean — that’s settled. The fence hotline is in place, which is good, but it’s a Band-Aid, not a relationship. People are going to be looking at that fence for years, and I need to remind myself that the response time matters less than what happens after the call. We’ve got contractors on site, work gloves in t

“Helena, I was just thinkin' about you—how you always tell it to me straight. The coffee pot's acting up again, and I swear it's the little things that get under my skin these days. How's your week treating you? Quiet minutes sound like gold right about now. I spent half the weekend staring at for-rent signs, trying to figure out if this neighborhood's still mine or if I'm just a ghost walking through someone else's plans. You always know how to ground a man. Maybe you're right—maybe stickin' ar
Omar Amici — Construction laborer — Uptown
